article_body: The kettle knows before I do. There is an hour, just after the light arrives and just before the day asks anything of me, when reading feels less like a task and more like weather. I keep a small stack for that hour. Nothing urgent, nothing that pings, nothing that refreshes itself while I look away. Just pages that waited for me, set in a type that does not hurry, on a surface that does not glow. The mornings are slower now, and so am I. I read a paragraph twice because I want to, not because I lost my place. The coffee goes cold and I let it. Somewhere a feed is filling up with things I will never need to know. Here, the page ends where it ends, and when I turn it, nothing else turns with it.
